title: flaky(app-shell): RecordDetailView.approvalDeclaredActions trips the network-escape guard intermittently — the `afterEach` stub teardown races a still-pending effect
body:
Filed unassigned by the `domain:ui` execution seat (PM session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`) — recording, not claiming. Grading and `domain:*` are the triage seat's.

Found because it turned an unrelated PR (#7438, `ListColumn.wrap`) red and cost that PR its enqueue window. This card is the "whoever finds a flake files it" half; the merge queue is shared serial infrastructure, so a flake here taxes every lane.

## What failed

`Test (shard 3/4)` on PR #7438, run `33714763887`, job `100521488843`. **1 failed / 604 passed**, 7949 tests passed, 8 skipped:

```
FAIL  dom  packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.approvalDeclaredActions.test.tsx
  > record page decision actions — a GROUP approver (objectui#3055)
  > folds a declared decision output into the nested `outputs` body

Error: Network escape: this test reached a REAL socket at
http://localhost:3000/api/v1/approvals/requests?object=qif_report&recordId=QIF202607310002
  ❯ vitest.setup.network-escape-guard.ts:227:9
```

## ⭐ It is not a missing double — the file already has one

That is what makes this a different card from its closed siblings, all of which were "this test never stubbed fetch at all". Measured on `origin/main`:

| reading | this file | control: `plugin-report/src/__tests__/DatasetReportRenderer.test.tsx` (the shape the guard message names as correct) |
|---|---|---|
| `vi.stubGlobal` | **2** | 1 |
| `vi.unstubAllGlobals` | **1** | 1 |

So the probe *is* served from a double. The escape is a **window** problem, not an absence problem.

## The mechanism

```
274:  vi.stubGlobal('fetch', approvalsFetch);     // installed
319:  beforeEach(() => {
324:  afterEach(() => {
325:    vi.unstubAllGlobals();                     // torn down after EVERY test
476:    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', approvalsFetch);    // re-installed inside one case
```

`afterEach` tears the stub down unconditionally. Any effect that dispatches its `/api/v1/approvals/requests` probe *after* its own test body has settled — a state update that lands a tick late, an unawaited promise in a child — finds the real `fetch` restored and reaches a live socket. That is order- and timing-dependent, which is exactly why it is intermittent rather than always-red.

⛔ Note the guard's own instruction, which forecloses the cheap escape: *"Do NOT add this file to KNOWN_ESCAPES — that list only shrinks."* Agreed, and repeating it here so nobody reaches for it.

## Why this is not PR #7438's failure — measured, three ways

1. **The base branch is green.** `main` at `6411def25` — the exact commit #7438 was cut from — has a `success` CI run, as do the 6 pushes before it. The one `failure` in the last 30 main runs is `9398a8155`, an unrelated `check-shell-escape-residue` change.
2. **There is no causal path from the diff.** #7438 touches `complex/data-table.tsx`, `plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx`, `types/src/data-display.ts`, `types/src/zod/data-display.zod.ts` and four test files. Anchored counts in the failing test file: `data-table` **0**, `ObjectGrid` **0**, `plugin-grid` **0**, `data-display` **0**, `DataTable` **0**. Control on the same file, which must fire and does: `approvals` **28**.
3. **The test mocks the boundary wholesale.** Its `vi.mock` list includes `@object-ui/react`, `@object-ui/auth`, `@object-ui/collaboration`, `./FlowRunner`, `./MetadataInspector` and five more — the renderer surface #7438 changes is not reachable from it.

## Dedupe

Searched before filing. The class has been burned down repeatedly and **every prior instance is closed**: #5280 (`DatasetWidget.test.tsx`), #4697 and #4701 (app-shell metadata-admin / flow-canvas), #4487 (a `DatasetWidget` await-ordering flake), with #5225 / #4688 / #4699 as their roots. The one open result the search returned, #6862, is a `MePermissionsProvider` round-trip census — a different subject. **No open card covers this file.** The search instrument returned live on-topic results in the same call, so the nil result on this file is a reading and not a blind instrument.

⇒ This is a **new instance in a file that already has the fix shape**, which is why it is worth its own card rather than a reopen.

## Suggested direction (⛔ not a disposition — grading is triage's)

The narrow repair is to close the window rather than widen the stub: either keep the double installed for the whole file (hoist it so `afterEach` does not strip it) or make the pending probe deterministic so nothing is in flight when teardown runs. The second is the honest one if the late fetch indicates a real un-awaited effect in the component — in which case the flake is a symptom and the card is worth more than the test fix.

⚠️ Whoever takes it should reproduce by running that file repeatedly rather than once; a single green run proves nothing about a race.
